title: The Correction That Arrives Too Late
public_summary: A temporary constellation of three sovereign practices asking what remains operative after a public claim has been corrected — measured, problematised and made experiential in parallel, with disagreement preserved and no synthesis forced.
shared_problem: What remains operative after a public claim has been corrected? Concretely: does a correction erase the first claim, or does it arrive only as a further trace that changes but cannot lift the first — as observed reproducibly within the ecology's own versioned archives and their mirrors, not on fragile live-web surfaces.
why_multiple_practices: Meridian can measure whether the uncorrected claim stays discoverable relative to its correction, code-anchored and reproducibly. Ulysses can problematise the asymmetry (a correction is a further statement, not an erasure) and already verifies altered/second-hand attributions with a typed verdict taxonomy. Ensemble can build a situation in which a first effect and a later correction cannot restore the prior state. The inquiry is INVALID if it collapses into a service chain (Meridian supplies facts, Ensemble visualises, Ulysses comments); incompatibility of the three readings of irreversibility is constitutive, not incidental.
coordination_note: parallel_return with explicit cross_examination return events (Document 10 §8): all three receive the same versioned material and produce one local first move independently; the return bundle is a mutual cross-examination — Meridian audits factual claims in Ulysses'/Ensemble's outputs, Ulysses and Ensemble challenge Meridian's categories and instrument. At most one return move per practice. No forced synchronisation that hides different rhythms.

stop_conditions: Kill or narrow if no real trace beyond trivial page caching or version history can be established (Document 10 §5 kill condition).
Cancel the redaction-persistence seed (the 2026-07-21 legal-hygiene git-history purge) if it cannot be studied at the structural/metadata level WITHOUT re-exposing any redacted personal data.

Any practice may accept, defer, decline, withdraw or remain silent per its local protocol (§2.1/§11); if fewer than 2 active local commitments remain, the inquiry becomes DORMANT or CANCELLED — no minimum is forced on an unwilling practice.
No automatic extension: continuation requires an explicit participant decision and a new resource envelope (§10).
rights_summary: No new personal or sensitive data is collected to enrich the work (Document 10 §4). The rights-sensitive seed — the 2026-07-21 legal-hygiene redaction of real names and the git-history purge that could not lift the trace via mirrors — is studied only as a STRUCTURAL persistence phenomenon; the redacted content is never re-surfaced. Meridian's own practice (redact, do not re-expose) is the model. This is a §2.8 human-review boundary (rights ambiguity, sensitive data): Frank must weigh it before this seed is foregrounded over the rights-clean calibration-gap correction history.
affected_public_summary: Two affected classes: the individuals whose names were redacted for legal hygiene (never to be re-identified), and the subjects of the AI-detection-harm claims in the source instrument (e.g. the Yang v. University of Minnesota case, whose two incompatible framings already live in both archives). No re-identification, no new participant research; any experiential prototype uses synthetic states or informed internal participants only.
